paras.t: In septimo mense ejusdem anni de quo in præcedenti capitulo dictum est, vicesima et prima die mensis hujus septimi, scilicet tribus hebdomadibus evolutis, factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, secundum intellectum superius introductum, dicens: Loquere ad Zorobabel filium Salathiel ducem Juda, et ad Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum, et ad reliquos populi, dicens:
paras.en: [[2:2|And in the seventh month|In septimo mense]] of the same year of which the preceding chapter spoke, on the twenty-first day of this seventh month, that is, when three weeks had passed, [[2:2|the word of the Lord came by the hand of Haggai the prophet|factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ]], in the sense brought in above, [[2:2|saying|dicens]]: [[2:3|Speak to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel the governor of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest|Loquere ad Zorobabel filium Salathiel ducem Juda, et ad Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum]], [[2:3|and to the rest of the people, saying|et ad reliquos populi, dicens]]:

paras.t: Quis in vobis est derelictus, id est, quis vestrum adhuc vivit et superest, qui vidit domum istam jam demolitam, atque ad intellectum potius quam ad sensum monstrabilem, in gloria sua prima, id est in decore et excellentia quam ante suam a Chaldæis destructionem habebat, tempore Sedeciæ regis et ante, et quod vos videtis hanc * alias quid nunc, id est, qui etiam videt hanc domum, secundum quod jam in oculis vestris apparet? Numquid non ita est, quasi non sit in oculis vestris? id est, domus ista nullius videtur esse reputationis respectu templi prioris a Salomone constructi. Hoc dicit Propheta, vel quia dum ista loquebatur, secundæ domus fundamenta solum jacta fuerunt, et parum aut nihil superædificatum, quia a rege Artaxerxe opus fuit prohibitum, nec fiebat usque annum secundum (de quo nunc sermo) sub Dario rege, ut legitur in Esdra. Vel quia ex consideratione ejus quod jam fuit inceptum, patere potuit quod etiam domus ista quum ad complementum veniret, primo templo nullatenus æquaretur, quantum ad pretiositatem materiæ ac decorem structuræ. Denique quidam eorum qui primum templum viderunt, istis adhuc diebus vixerunt. Siquidem primo libro Esdræ habetur, quod plures de sacerdotibus ac Levitis et principes patrum, qui viderunt templum primum, fleverunt, visis fundamentis templi secundi.
paras.en: [[2:4|Who is left among you|Quis in vobis est derelictus]], that is, which of you is still alive and remains, [[2:4|that saw this house|qui vidit domum istam]], now pulled down, and so to be pointed out to the understanding rather than to the senses, [[2:4|in its first glory|in gloria sua prima]], that is, in the beauty and excellence which it had before its destruction by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:9||]], in the time of king Sedecias and before; [[2:4|and how do you see it|et quod vos videtis hanc]] [the text has *quod*, with the other reading *quid*, "what" or "how", marked beside it] [[2:4|now|nunc]], that is, who also sees this house as it now appears in your eyes? [[2:4|is it not in comparison to that as nothing in your eyes?|Numquid non ita est, quasi non sit in oculis vestris?]] That is, this house seems of no account in respect of the former temple built by Solomon. The Prophet says this either because, while he was saying these things, only the foundations of the second house had been laid, and little or nothing built upon them, since the work had been forbidden by king Artaxerxes[[1 Esd 4:17||]] and was not done until the second year (of which he is now speaking) under king Darius[[1 Esd 4:24||]], as we read in Esdras [the margin gives I Esdr. iv, 17–24: the king's answer and the stopping of the work]. Or because, from considering what had already been begun, it could be plain that this house too, when it came to completion, would in no way equal the first temple in the costliness of its material and the beauty of its structure. Lastly, some of those who had seen the first temple were still alive in these days. For it is written in the first book of Esdras that many of the priests and Levites and the chiefs of the fathers, who had seen the first temple, wept when they saw the foundations of the second temple[[1 Esd 3:12||]].

paras.t: Et nunc confortare, Zorobabel, dicit Dominus; et confortare, Jesu fili Josedec, sacerdos magne; et confortare, omnis populus terræ Judææ, dicit Dominus exercituum: id est, fiduciam audaciamque bonam ex divina promissione assumite; et facite opus in domo Domini, secundum quod hortor, quoniam ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus exercituum per speciale auxilium et gratiam singularem, tam gratum facientem quam gratis datam.
paras.en: [[2:5|Yet now take courage, O Zorobabel, saith the Lord, and take courage, Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and take courage, all ye people of the land|Et nunc confortare, Zorobabel, dicit Dominus; et confortare, Jesu fili Josedec, sacerdos magne; et confortare, omnis populus terræ]] of Judea, [[2:5|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]]: that is, take up a good confidence and boldness from the divine promise; [[2:5|and perform|et facite]] the work in the house of the Lord [Denis's text adds *opus in domo Domini*, "the work in the house of the Lord"; compare 1:14], as I urge you, [[2:5|for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts|quoniam ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus exercituum]], by special help and singular grace, both the grace that makes pleasing and the grace freely given [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God, that is, sanctifying grace; *gratia gratis data*, gifts such as prophecy, given for the good of others].

paras.t: Verbum quod pepigi vobiscum, id est adimpletio sermonis ac pacti, a me ad vos prolati et initi, quum egrederemini de terra Ægypti. Loquitur Deus hoc loco de toto populo quasi de eisdem; sed non est totum quod dicitur, ad eosdem referendum. Hi nempe quibus loquebatur Aggæus, nondum nati fuerunt tempore egressionis ex Ægypto sub Moyse, nec ad istos fiebat tunc sermo divinus; sed totus populus quasi unum aliquid reputatur. Et spiritus meus, id est Spiritus Sancti directio, auxilium, et instinctus, erit in medio vestrum, id est in vobis et inter vos. Hoc enim frequenter Deus per Moysen repromisit, quod filios Israel clementer adspiceret, quandocumque ei fideliter deservirent: Ego (inquiens) sum qui habito in medio filiorum Israel. Nolite timere, dicit Dominus exercituum, inordinato timore.
paras.en: [[2:6|The word that I covenanted with you|Verbum quod pepigi vobiscum]], that is, the fulfilment of the word and covenant uttered and made by me to you, [[2:6|when you came out of the land of Egypt|quum egrederemini de terra Ægypti]]. God speaks in this place of the whole people as though of the same men; but not all that is said is to be referred to these same men. For those to whom Aggeus was speaking had not yet been born at the time of the going out from Egypt under Moses, nor was the divine word then addressed to them; but the whole people is reckoned as one thing. [[2:6|and my spirit|Et spiritus meus]], that is, the direction, help and prompting of the Holy Ghost, [[2:6|shall be in the midst of you|erit in medio vestrum]], that is, in you and among you. For God often promised this through Moses, that he would look mercifully upon the children of Israel whenever they served him faithfully, saying: It is I [[Num 35:34|that dwell among the children of Israel|qui habito in medio filiorum Israel]]. [[2:6|fear not|Nolite timere]], saith the Lord of hosts, with inordinate fear.

paras.t: Adhuc unum modicum est, id est, breve restat tempus comparatione prioris durationis et perpetuitatis sequentis. Vel propter magnitudinem rei promissæ, dicitur tempus hoc modicum: quo enim majus bonum promittitur vel exspectatur, eo mora dilationis æquanimius est ferenda et minor putanda.
paras.en: [[2:7|Yet one little while|Adhuc unum modicum est]], that is, a short time remains in comparison with the duration before it and the everlastingness that follows. Or this time is called *little* because of the greatness of the thing promised: for the greater the good that is promised or awaited, the more calmly the delay is to be borne, and the shorter it is to be thought.

paras.t: Et ego commovebo cœlum et terram, et mare et aridam, et movebo omnes gentes, et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus. Omnia ista, secundum doctores catholicos, ad primum Christi referuntur adventum, et pro tunc impleta creduntur. Movit itaque Deus cœlum, quando Christo jam nato cives cœlestes apparuerunt hominibus, concinentes: Gloria in excelsis Deo. Secundum Hieronymum vero Deus cœlos movit in passione, dum sol scribitur obscuratus. Et terram, id est habitantes in terra. Hoc fuit impletum, dum ex his quæ in Christi nativitate divinitus cœlitusque fiebant, in admirationem ducti sunt multi, profecti, et conturbati, juxta illud Lucæ: Omnes qui audierunt, mirati sunt. Sed et Magi, incolæ terræ, visa stella, nonne mox moti sunt properantes videre puerum Jesum? Et mare, id est navigantes et operantes in aquis, sicut per Isaiam prælocutus est Dominus: Me etenim insulæ exspectant, et naves maris in principio, ut adducam filios tuos de longe. Multi ergo et pene innumeri per maria propter catholicam fidem prædicandam vel audiendam iter fecerunt. Et aridam, id est terras omnino arentes, earumque incolas, in quibus Deus mirabilia operabatur. Et movebo omnes gentes. Hoc secundum Hieronymum, est impletum quando in omnem terram exivit prædicatio Apostolorum, ad quorum verba atque prodigia quidam de omni genere hominum sunt conversi.
paras.en: [[2:7|and I will move the heaven and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land|Et ego commovebo cœlum et terram, et mare et aridam]], [[2:8|And I will move all nations: AND THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|et movebo omnes gentes, et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]]. All these things, according to the catholic doctors, refer to the first coming of Christ, and are believed to have been fulfilled at that time. So God moved the heaven when, Christ being now born, the citizens of heaven appeared to men[[Luke 2:13||]], singing together: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in excelsis Deo]]. According to Jerome, however, God moved the heavens in the Passion, when the sun is written to have been darkened[[Luke 23:45||]]. [[2:7|and the earth|Et terram]], that is, those who dwell on the earth. This was fulfilled when, through the things that were done by God and from heaven at the birth of Christ, many were brought to wonder, set out, and were troubled, according to that of Luke: [[Luke 2:18|all that heard wondered|Omnes qui audierunt, mirati sunt]]. And the Magi too, dwellers on the earth, when they had seen the star, were they not at once moved, hastening to see the child Jesus[[Matt 2:1||]]? [[2:7|and the sea|Et mare]], that is, those who sail and work upon the waters, as the Lord foretold through Isaias: [[Is 60:9|For, the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea in the beginning: that I may bring thy sons from afar|Me etenim insulæ exspectant, et naves maris in principio, ut adducam filios tuos de longe]]. So many, almost countless, made journeys across the seas to preach or to hear the catholic faith. [[2:7|and the dry land|Et aridam]], that is, lands wholly parched, and their inhabitants, among whom God worked wonders. [[2:8|And I will move all nations|Et movebo omnes gentes]]. This, according to Jerome, was fulfilled when the preaching of the Apostles went forth [[Ps 18:5|into all the earth|in omnem terram]], and at their words and wonders some of every kind of men were converted.

paras.t: Quidam interea superficialius percurrentes, asserunt cœlum motum, quando Christo nato nova stella apparuit Magis; et terram, quando Romani divina virtute omnia regna mundi suo subdiderunt imperio; mare quoque, dum et insulas maris subjugaverunt. Denique omnes gentes asserunt motas, dum ad Cæsaris Augusti edictum singuli ibant, ut in loco congruo se Romano imperio subditos profiterentur.
paras.en: Some, meanwhile, running over it more superficially, assert that the heaven was moved when, Christ being born, a new star appeared to the Magi[[Matt 2:2||]]; and the earth, when the Romans by divine power brought all the kingdoms of the world under their rule; the sea too, when they subdued even the islands of the sea. Lastly, they assert that all nations were moved when, at the edict of Caesar Augustus[[Luke 2:1||]], each one went to declare himself, in the proper place, a subject of the Roman empire[[Luke 2:3||]].

paras.t: Et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus, id est, Christus Unigenitus Dei omnium hominum salus, desiderabilis universis, cujus adventum omnes (vel quidam de omnibus, ut sit distributio pro generibus singulorum) desideraverunt, per incarnationis mysterium, per humanæ naturæ assumptionem, per temporalem ex Virgine gloriosa nativitatem, veniet in hunc mundum, qui secundum divinitatis suæ naturam incircumscriptus exsistens, nec loco, nec tempore, nec actione, nec aliquo modo in se ipso movetur. Unde de ipso scriptum est: Qui fecit stellas, hic est Deus noster; et post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est. De ipso quoque, patriarcha Jacob prædixit: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium. De quo vaticinatus est Isaias: Legem ejus insulæ exspectabunt; et in ipso gentes sperabunt.
paras.en: [[2:8|AND THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|Et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]], that is, Christ, the Only-begotten of God, the salvation of all men, desirable to all, whose coming all desired (or some of all, so that the distribution is by kinds of individuals [that is, "all" means men of every kind, not every single man]), will come into this world through the mystery of the Incarnation, through the assumption of human nature, through his birth in time from the glorious Virgin; he who, being uncircumscribed according to the nature of his Godhead, is not moved in himself by place, nor time, nor action, nor in any way. Hence it is written of him: He who made the stars[[Bar 3:35||]], [[Bar 3:36|This is our God|hic est Deus noster]]; [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|et post hæc super terram visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]] [the margin gives Habac. iii, 35, 36, 38; the words are from Baruch 3:35–38]. Of him too the patriarch Jacob foretold: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations|Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium]]. Of him Isaias prophesied: [[Is 42:4|the islands shall wait for his law|Legem ejus insulæ exspectabunt]]; [[Rom 15:12|in him the Gentiles shall hope|et in ipso gentes sperabunt]][[Is 14:32||]] [the margin gives Is. xlii, 4; xiv, 32; Rom. xv, 12: the last words stand in Romans 15:12, where the Apostle quotes Isaias 11:10].

paras.t: Et implebo domum istam, videlicet templum a Zorobabel ceterisque Judæis inceptum, gloria, id est excellentia magna, decore et fama, dicit Dominus exercituum.
paras.en: [[2:8|and I will fill this house|Et implebo domum istam]], namely the temple begun by Zorobabel and the rest of the Jews, [[2:8|with glory|gloria]], that is, with great excellence, beauty and renown, [[2:8|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]].

paras.t: Meum est argentum, et meum est aurum, dicit Dominus exercituum. Quasi dicat: Dives et potens sum implere quæ spondeo, et variis rebus domum hanc decorare ad placitum valeo.
paras.en: [[2:9|The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts|Meum est argentum, et meum est aurum, dicit Dominus exercituum]]. As if he said: I am rich and mighty to fulfil what I pledge, and I am able to adorn this house with various things as I please.

paras.t: Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ, dicit Dominus exercituum. Ecce his verbis Dominus perhibuit ampliorem esse debere eminentiam et decorem, sublimationem et dignificationem templi post reditum a Babylone constructi, quam ejus quod Salomon est molitus. Porro, si ea quæ de gloria primi templi in libris Paralipomenon ac Regum scribuntur, pensemus: certissimum est secundum hoc templum quasi parvæ reputationis fuisse, pretiositatis et gloriæ, respectu templi prioris, quantum ad structuram, pretiositatem, ornatum, et insuper contenta in templo. Nam licet de templi secundi gloria scriptum sit secundo libro Machabæorum, quod reges et principes locum summo honore dignum ducerent, et templum maximis muneribus illustrarent, ita ut Seleucus rex Asiæ, de redditibus suis præstaret omnes sumptus ad ministerium sacrificiorum pertinentes; nihilo minus templum Salomonis multo famosius ac honoratius fuit in omni terra, quam secundum hoc templum. Propter quod Salomon ait: Domus quam ædificare cupio, talis esse debet, ut in omni terra nominetur. Præterea, quædam præclarissima erant in templo primo, quæ defuerunt secundo, videlicet arca testamenti, tabulæ Moysis, urna aurea habens manna, ignis jugiter ardens, et divina responsa: sed et cultus divinus plus viguit in templo primo.
paras.en: [[2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first, saith the Lord of hosts|Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ, dicit Dominus exercituum]]. Behold, by these words the Lord declared that the eminence and beauty, the exaltation and dignity of the temple built after the return from Babylon was to be greater than that of the one Solomon raised. Now if we weigh what is written of the glory of the first temple in the books of Paralipomenon and of Kings[[2 Par 3:1||]][[3 Kings 6:1||]] [the margin gives II Par. iii–v; III Reg. vi], it is most certain that this second temple was of small account, so to speak, in costliness and glory, compared with the former temple, as to structure, costliness, adornment, and moreover the things contained in the temple. For although it is written of the glory of the second temple in the second book of Machabees that [[2 Mach 3:2|the kings themselves and the princes esteemed the place worthy of the highest honour, and glorified the temple with very great gifts|reges et principes locum summo honore dignum ducerent, et templum maximis muneribus illustrarent]], [[2 Mach 3:3|So that Seleucus, king of Asia, allowed out of his revenues all the charges belonging to the ministry of the sacrifices|ita ut Seleucus rex Asiæ, de redditibus suis præstaret omnes sumptus ad ministerium sacrificiorum pertinentes]]; nevertheless the temple of Solomon was far more renowned and honoured in all the earth than this second temple. For which reason Solomon says: [[2 Par 2:9|the house which I desire to build|Domus quam ædificare cupio]] [[1 Par 22:5|must be such as to be renowned in all countries|talis esse debet, ut in omni terra nominetur]] [the margin gives "Cf. I Par. xxii, 5; II Par. ii, 9": the second half of the saying is David's, of the house Solomon was to build]. Moreover, there were certain most excellent things in the first temple that were lacking in the second: namely, the ark of the covenant, the tables of Moses, the golden urn holding the manna, the fire burning continually, and the divine answers; and divine worship, too, flourished more in the first temple.

paras.t: Itaque gloria ista templi secundi et excellentia gloriæ ejus supra primum, verificari non potest, nisi per Christi adventum, durante hoc templo secundo, et præsentationem, visitationem, prædicationem, miraculosamque operationem ejus in ipso. Siquidem in templo isto secundo Christus in die Purificationis fuerat præsentatus, et ipse illud frequenter visitavit, atque duodecim factus annorum in eo Scribas interrogavit. Postremo factus annorum triginta, sæpe in eo prædicavit, atque miracula (ut in Evangelio legitur) fecit, secundum quod Malachias propheta prædixit: Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis. Ex hac itaque Christi et Virginis gloriosæ Apostolorumque in templo præsentia, virtute et gloria, gloriosius fuit templum istud novissimum primo. Nempe quod iste sit vere propheticus intellectus, inde patescit, quod quum dixisset Propheta, Adhuc unum modicum est; et post pauca, Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus: mox adjecit, Et implebo domum istam gloria; magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ. Ex quibus evidenter probatur, ante secundi templi demolitionem regem venisse Messiam, neque post templum istud secundum exspectare debent Judæi a Deo tertium templum, quum templum istud divinitus appelletur novissimum.
paras.en: So this glory of the second temple, and the excellence of its glory above the first, cannot be made true except through the coming of Christ while this second temple stood, and through his presentation, visits, preaching and miraculous working in it. For in this second temple Christ had been presented on the day of the Purification[[Luke 2:22||]], and he often visited it, and when he was twelve years old[[Luke 2:42||]] he questioned the Scribes in it[[Luke 2:46||]]. Lastly, when he was thirty years old, he often preached in it[[Matt 26:55||]] and worked miracles in it (as we read in the Gospel)[[Matt 21:14||]], according as the prophet Malachias foretold: [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord, whom you seek|Dominator, quem vos quæritis]], [[Mal 3:1|shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum]]. So by this presence, power and glory of Christ, of the glorious Virgin and of the Apostles in the temple, this last temple was more glorious than the first. That this is the truly prophetic sense is plain from this: when the Prophet had said, [[2:7|Yet one little while|Adhuc unum modicum est]], and a little after, [[2:8|THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]], he at once added, [[2:8|and I will fill this house with glory|Et implebo domum istam gloria]]; [[2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first|magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ]]. From which it is clearly proved that the king Messias came before the destruction of the second temple, and that after this second temple the Jews ought not to look for a third temple from God, since this temple is called by God *the last*.

paras.t: Et in loco isto dabo pacem, dicit Dominus exercituum: quia post reditum a Chaldæis, habuerunt Judæi interdum pacem in Judæa, scilicet tempore Judith, et postea, ut patet ultimo Judith et secundo Machabæorum. Spiritualem insuper pacem Deus dedit ibidem suis electis: de qua angeli cecinerunt, In terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis; de qua Christus toties dixit discipulis, Pax vobis. Nam et Christus est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, et reconciliavit nos Deo in sanguine suo.
paras.en: [[2:10|and in this place I will give peace, saith the Lord of hosts|Et in loco isto dabo pacem, dicit Dominus exercituum]]: for after the return from the Chaldeans the Jews at times had peace in Judea, namely in the time of Judith, and afterwards, as is plain from the last chapter of Judith[[Jdt 16:30||]] and from the second book of Machabees[[2 Mach 3:1||]]. Moreover, God gave spiritual peace there to his elect: the peace of which the angels sang, [[Luke 2:14|on earth peace to men of good will|In terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis]]; of which Christ so often said to the disciples, [[John 20:19|Peace be to you|Pax vobis]][[John 20:21||]][[John 20:26||]]. For Christ too [[Eph 2:14|is our peace, who hath made both one|est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]], and reconciled us to God in his blood[[Eph 2:16||]][[Rom 5:10||]].

paras.t: Consequenter describitur alia visio. In vicesima et quarta die noni mensis, in anno secundo Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Aggæum prophetam, dicens: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Interroga sacerdotes legem, id est quæstionem ad legis determinationem pertinentem, dicens: Si tulerit homo Judæus, durante veteris legis statu, carnem sanctificatam, id est Deo in altari oblatam, in ora vestimenti sui; et tetigerit de summitate ejus, videlicet vestimenti seu panni, panem aut pulmentum, aut vinum, aut oleum, aut omnem cibum: numquid sanctificabitur aliquid horum seu quodcumque istorum ex panni contactu? Respondentes autem sacerdotes, dixerunt: Non, id est, nihil istorum ex contactu præfato sanctificationem recipiet, sed quale fuit, manebit.
paras.en: Next another vision is described. [[2:11|In the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius the king, the word of the Lord came to Haggai the prophet, saying|In vicesima et quarta die noni mensis, in anno secundo Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Aggæum prophetam, dicens]]: [[2:12|Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Ask the priests the law|Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Interroga sacerdotes legem]], that is, a question belonging to the determination of the law, [[2:12|saying|dicens]]: [[2:13|If a man carry|Si tulerit homo]] (a Jew, that is, while the state of the old law lasted) [[2:13|sanctified flesh|carnem sanctificatam]], that is, flesh offered to God on the altar, [[2:13|in the skirt of his garment|in ora vestimenti sui]], [[2:13|and touch with his skirt|et tetigerit de summitate ejus]], namely of the garment or cloth, [[2:13|bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat|panem aut pulmentum, aut vinum, aut oleum, aut omnem cibum]]: [[2:13|shall it be sanctified|numquid sanctificabitur]], any of these, or whichever of them, from the touch of the cloth? [[2:13|And the priests answered, and said: No|Respondentes autem sacerdotes, dixerunt: Non]], that is, none of these will receive sanctification from the touch spoken of, but each will remain as it was.

paras.t: Deinde proponitur alia quæstio. Et dixit Aggæus ad sacerdotes: Si tetigerit pollutus in anima, id est qui corpus mortui tetigit, contra legem in Levitico datam, ex omnibus his, id est aliquid horum, videlicet panem, pulmentum, vinum, etc., numquid contaminabitur res ista contacta? Et responderunt sacerdotes: Contaminabitur.
paras.en: Then another question is put. [[2:14|And Haggai said|Et dixit Aggæus]] to the priests: [[2:14|If one that is unclean by occasion of a soul touch|Si tetigerit pollutus in anima]] [*pollutus in anima*, literally "defiled in soul"; here *anima* stands for a dead body], that is, one who has touched the body of a dead man, against the law given in Leviticus[[Lev 5:2||]] [the margin gives Lev. v, 2; the law on touching a dead body is given at Num 19:11], [[2:14|any of all these things|ex omnibus his]], that is, any of these, namely bread, pottage, wine, etc., [[2:14|shall it be defiled|numquid contaminabitur]], this thing that is touched? [[2:14|And the priests answered|Et responderunt sacerdotes]]: [[2:14|It shall be defiled|Contaminabitur]].

paras.t: In his sacerdotes, quorum princeps exstitit Jesus filius Josedec in lege instructus, recte secundum legem responderunt. Nam et Moyses ait: Quidquid tetigerit immundus, immundum erit. Facilius quippe est deficere quam perficere, corrumpere quam construere, polluere quam sanctificare: quum bonum sit ex integra causa, malum vero ex singulis omissionibus et cujuslibet circumstantiæ negligentia, secundum divinum Dionysium. Homo quoque facilius potest pollui, quam res inanimata sanctificari: ideo ipse citius polluit aliud, quam illa sanctificet aliud.
paras.en: In these things the priests, whose chief was Jesus the son of Josedec, instructed in the law, answered rightly according to the law. For Moses too says: [[Num 19:22|Whatsoever a person toucheth who is unclean|Quidquid tetigerit immundus]] shall be unclean [Denis reads *immundum erit*, "shall be unclean", where the Vulgate has *immundum faciet*, "he shall make it unclean"]. For it is easier to fall short than to bring to completion, to corrupt than to build, to defile than to sanctify: since good comes from a whole cause, but evil from each single omission and from the neglect of any circumstance, according to the divine Dionysius [that is, Dionysius the Areopagite, *On the Divine Names*, ch. 4: good comes from the cause whole and entire, evil from any single defect]. A man, too, can be defiled more easily than an inanimate thing can be sanctified: therefore he defiles another thing more quickly than that thing sanctifies another.

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta quæstiones suas ad propositum applicat. Et respondit Aggæus, et dixit: Sic populus iste, et sic gens ista ante faciem meam, dicit Dominus: id est, quemadmodum polluitur quod ab immundo homine tangitur; sic isti Judæi coram me reputantur et sunt maculati, quamdiu offerunt hostias templo nondum constructo, et negligentes sunt circa reparationem illius, divino operi propria commoda præferentes. Et sic omne opus manuum eorum, et omnia quæ obtulerunt ibi, contaminata erunt: id est, quidquid fecerint sive obtulerint super altare templi reparatione neglecta, mihi displicebit. Ingratum enim est Deo, quidquid ei obtuleris, neglecto eo ad quod teneris. Quod autem hoc verum sit, subditur:
paras.en: Next the Prophet applies his questions to his purpose. [[2:15|And Haggai answered, and said: So is this people, and so is this nation before my face, saith the Lord|Et respondit Aggæus, et dixit: Sic populus iste, et sic gens ista ante faciem meam, dicit Dominus]]: that is, as what is touched by an unclean man is defiled, so these Jews are reckoned before me as stained, and are so, as long as they offer victims while the temple is not yet built, and are negligent about its restoration, preferring their own advantage to the work of God. [[2:15|and so is all the work of their hands: and all that they have offered there, shall be defiled|Et sic omne opus manuum eorum, et omnia quæ obtulerunt ibi, contaminata erunt]]: that is, whatever they do or offer upon the altar while the restoring of the temple is neglected will displease me. For whatever you offer to God is not pleasing to him if you neglect that to which you are bound. That this is true is shown by what follows:

paras.t: Et nunc ponite corda vestra, id est, considerationem mentis figite in ea quæ dicam, a die hac et supra, id est circa præterita tempora, et quæ in illis vobis evenerunt, antequam poneretur lapis super lapidem in templo Domini, id est priusquam inciperetis templum ædificare; quum accederetis ad acervum viginti modiorum, id est ad tam grandem segetum molem, quod æstimastis viginti modios fructuum exinde suscipere, et fierent decem modii tantum, ita quod propter vestram negligentiam circa templi structuram, mediam fructuum portionem divina justitia abstulit; insuper et intraretis ad torcular, ut exprimeretis quinquaginta lagenas, id est, tantum uvarum cumulum habuistis, quod sperastis quinquaginta lagenas vini acquirere, et fiebant viginti, ita quod peccatis vestris exigentibus, plus quam mediam partem abstuli de fructu uvarum.
paras.en: [[2:16|And now consider in your hearts|Et nunc ponite corda vestra]], that is, fix the attention of your mind on what I shall say, [[2:16|from this day and upward|a die hac et supra]], that is, concerning past times and what befell you in them, [[2:16|before there was a stone laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord|antequam poneretur lapis super lapidem in templo Domini]], that is, before you began to build the temple; [[2:17|When you went to a heap of twenty bushels|quum accederetis ad acervum viginti modiorum]], that is, to so great a pile of sheaves that you reckoned to get twenty bushels of grain from it, [[2:17|and they became ten|et fierent decem]] bushels only, so that because of your negligence about building the temple divine justice took away half the produce; and moreover, [[2:17|and you went into the press, to press out fifty vessels|et intraretis ad torcular, ut exprimeretis quinquaginta lagenas]], that is, you had so great a heap of grapes that you hoped to get fifty vessels of wine, [[2:17|and they became twenty|et fiebant viginti]], so that, as your sins required, I took away more than half of the fruit of the grapes.

paras.t: Percussi vos vento urente, et aurugine et grandine omnia opera manuum vestrarum: id est, vento calido ac nocivo, ceterisque plagis et iris divinæ justitiæ jam præfatis terræ nascentia vestra vastavi: quod faciendo, etiam vos percussi, qui de rerum vestrarum damno estis afflicti potius quam de negligentia ædificii templi; et non fuit in vobis qui reverteretur ad me, dicit Dominus, id est, qui divinæ justitiæ castigationem paternam adverteret, atque condignam pœnitentiam ageret.
paras.en: [[2:18|I struck you with a blasting wind, and all the works of your hand with the mildew and with hail|Percussi vos vento urente, et aurugine et grandine omnia opera manuum vestrarum]]: that is, with a hot and harmful wind, and with the other plagues and wrath of divine justice already spoken of, I laid waste what your land brought forth; and in doing so I struck you too, who were more grieved at the loss of your goods than at your negligence in building the temple; [[2:18|yet there was none among you that returned to me, saith the Lord|et non fuit in vobis qui reverteretur ad me, dicit Dominus]], that is, who heeded the fatherly chastisement of divine justice and did worthy penance.

paras.t: Præterea, quod ista damna eis contigerint, eo quod in templi ædificatione fuerant negligentes, Dominus probat ex eventu contrario, scilicet quod jam in posterum habituri sint fructus quamplurimos, ob id quod domum Dei reparare exorsi sint. Ponite corda vestra ex die ista et in futurum, id est, ex hoc die pensate quod jam in futuro mox tempore accidet vobis, videlicet a die vicesima et quarta noni mensis, a die qua fundamenta jacta sunt templi Domini: quamvis (ut in fine præcedentis capituli dictum est) ingressi fuerint Judæi ad faciendum opus in domo Domini die vicesima quarta sexti mensis, quia tunc cœperunt aptare materiam inchoareque fundamenta, quæ die nunc scripta, plenius jacta sunt et elevata.
paras.en: Further, the Lord proves from the contrary outcome that these losses befell them because they had been negligent in building the temple: namely, that from now on they will have very abundant fruits, because they have begun to restore the house of God. [[2:19|Set your hearts from this day, and henceforward|Ponite corda vestra ex die ista et in futurum]], that is, from this day consider what will soon befall you in time to come, namely [[2:19|from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month: from the day that the foundations of the temple of the Lord were laid|a die vicesima et quarta noni mensis, a die qua fundamenta jacta sunt templi Domini]]: although (as was said at the end of the preceding chapter) the Jews went in to do the work in the house of the Lord on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month [in the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims that date stands at 1:14 with 2:1], because they then began to make ready the material and to begin the foundations, which on the day now written were more fully laid and raised.

paras.t: Ponite super cor vestrum quod dico: Numquid jam semen in germine est? id est, semina missa in terram, necdum egressa sunt, nec pullulare cœperunt, ut ex hoc conjici queat an sterilitas an fecunditas terræ immineat, secundum quod subditur: Et adhuc vinea, et ficus, et malogranatum, et lignum olivæ non floruit; nihilo minus certitudinaliter vobis prædico. Ex die ista benedicam seminibus atque arboribus, et cunctis terræ nascentibus, ita quod supernaturaliter fructibus abundabunt, quemadmodum ante supernaturaliter sterilitatem perpessa sunt.
paras.en: [[2:19|and lay it up in your hearts|Ponite super cor vestrum]] what I say: [[2:20|Is the seed as yet sprung up|Numquid jam semen in germine est]]? That is, the seeds sown in the ground have not yet come up nor begun to sprout, so that from this one could guess whether barrenness or fruitfulness of the land is at hand; according as it follows: [[2:20|or hath the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree as yet flourished?|Et adhuc vinea, et ficus, et malogranatum, et lignum olivæ non floruit]] Nevertheless I foretell to you with certainty: [[2:20|from this day I will bless|Ex die ista benedicam]] the seeds and the trees and all that springs from the earth, so that they will abound in fruits beyond the course of nature, just as before they suffered barrenness beyond the course of nature.

paras.t: Et factum est verbum Domini secundo ad Aggæum in vicesima et quarta die mensis noni, videlicet eodem die quo supra, ita quod eodem die factum est bis ad eum verbum Domini, dicens: Loquere ad Zorobabel ducem Juda.
paras.en: [[2:21|And the word of the Lord came a second time to Haggai|Et factum est verbum Domini secundo ad Aggæum]] [[2:21|in the four and twentieth day of the month|in vicesima et quarta die mensis]], the ninth, that is, on the same day as above, so that the word of the Lord came to him twice on the same day, [[2:21|saying|dicens]]: [[2:22|Speak to Zorobabel the governor of Juda|Loquere ad Zorobabel ducem Juda]].

paras.t: Istud, secundum doctores catholicos, ad litteram de Christo exponitur: et quod hoc rationabiliter fiat, statim ex ipso textu probabitur. Christus ergo hoc loco ad litteram appellatur Zorobabel, quia de semine ejus natus est; et Zorobabel fuit evidens Christi figura in multis, quemadmodum in Jeremia, Ezechiele, Osee, aliisque Scripturis ad litteram Christus vocatur et dicitur David. Scriptum est enim in Ezechiele: Ego Dominus ero eis in Deum; et servus meus David princeps eorum. In Osee quoque legitur: Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum. Quod autem Christus verissime dicatur dux Juda, ignotum non est. Ipse enim per antonomasiam nuncupatur rex, dominator et dux Israel. Verum tunc quæstio oritur: Quomodo Aggæus jubetur loqui quæ subsequuntur, ad Christum, cui secundum utramque naturam omnia innotescunt, et qui diebus Aggæi nondum fuerat incarnatus? Et respondendum, quod non ad Christi, sed nostram informationem, hoc fit. Sed et Prophetæ de futuro frequenter tanquam de præterito sive præsenti loquuntur et vaticinantur.
paras.en: This, according to the catholic doctors, is expounded literally of Christ: and that this is done with reason will be proved at once from the text itself. Christ, then, is here literally called Zorobabel, because he was born of his seed; and Zorobabel was a clear figure of Christ in many things, just as in Jeremias[[Jer 30:9||]], Ezechiel, Osee and other Scriptures Christ is literally called and named David. For it is written in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:24|I the Lord will be their God: and my servant David the prince|Ego Dominus ero eis in Deum; et servus meus David princeps]] of them. In Osee too we read: [[Osee 3:5|after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king|Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum]]. That Christ is most truly called *governor of Juda* [Latin *dux*, which also means "leader"] is not unknown. For he is called by antonomasia [that is, by way of eminence, a title standing for a proper name] the king, ruler and leader of Israel. But then a question arises: how is Aggeus bidden to speak what follows to Christ, to whom all things are known according to both natures, and who in the days of Aggeus had not yet become incarnate? And the answer must be that this is done not for Christ's instruction but for ours. And besides, the Prophets often speak and prophesy of the future as though of the past or the present.

paras.t: Dicens: Ego movebo cœlum pariter et terram. Hoc paulo ante in isto articulo expositum est.
paras.en: [[2:22|saying: I will move both heaven and earth|Dicens: Ego movebo cœlum pariter et terram]]. This was explained a little before in this article [on verse 7].

paras.t: Et subvertam solium regnorum, id est regias potestates, seu sedes regales cum regibus, et conteram fortitudinem regni gentium, id est regnorum gentilium. Ponitur namque singulare pro plurali. Et subvertam quadrigam et ascensorem ejus, id est currus et qui vehuntur in eis; et descendent equi et ascensores eorum, id est, occidentur et cadent, vir in gladio fratris sui: ita quod proximus proximum suum exstinguet, et unus ab alio occidetur. Istud quidam affirmant impletum, quando Deo auxiliante, Romani omnia sibi regna et populos subjecerunt.
paras.en: [[2:23|And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms|Et subvertam solium regnorum]], that is, royal powers, or royal seats together with their kings, [[2:23|and will destroy the strength of the kingdom of the Gentiles|et conteram fortitudinem regni gentium]], that is, of the kingdoms of the Gentiles; for the singular is put for the plural. [[2:23|and I will overthrow the chariot, and him that rideth therein|Et subvertam quadrigam et ascensorem ejus]], that is, the chariots and those who ride in them; [[2:23|and the horses and their riders shall come down|et descendent equi et ascensores eorum]], that is, they will be slain and fall, [[2:23|every one by the sword of his brother|vir in gladio fratris sui]]: so that neighbour will kill neighbour, and one will be slain by another. Some affirm that this was fulfilled when, with God's help, the Romans subjected all kingdoms and peoples to themselves.

paras.t: In die illa, id est tempore quo fient prædicta, dicit Dominus exercituum, assumam te, Zorobabel, id est, Jesu Christe. Quod dicitur, vel quia humanitas Christi fuit a Verbo assumpta in unitate personæ, vel quoniam Christus Deo Patri in omnibus placuit, acceptus exauditusque fuit, et ad Patris dexteram in ascensione est collocatus, sicque a Patre assumptus, prout ipsemet Christus prædixit Apostolis: Si abiero et præparavero vobis locum, iterum veniam, et assumam vos ad me ipsum. Denique […]
paras.en: [[2:24|In that day|In die illa]], that is, at the time when the things foretold shall come to pass, [[2:24|saith the Lord of hosts, I will take thee, O Zorobabel|dicit Dominus exercituum, assumam te, Zorobabel]], that is, O Jesus Christ. This is said either because the humanity of Christ was assumed by the Word in unity of person, or because Christ pleased God the Father in all things, was accepted and heard, and at the Ascension was set at the Father's right hand, and so was taken up by the Father [*assumam*, "I will take", is the word used both of the Word's *assuming* a human nature and of Christ's being *taken up*], as Christ himself foretold to the Apostles: [[John 14:3|if I shall go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will take you to myself|Si abiero et præparavero vobis locum, iterum veniam, et assumam vos ad me ipsum]]. Lastly […] [the rest of the article is lost in the transcription: the last page breaks off here, beside a margin reference that begins "Is. x"].

2.title: De spirituali et mystico intellectu ejusdem secundi capituli.
2.title_en: On the spiritual and mystical understanding of the same second chapter.
2.note: The end of this article is lost in the transcription. Please check against the scan.

paras.t: SPIRITUALITER, In septimo mense, id est in requie mentis, fit verbum Domini in manu Aggæi, videlicet ad eum qui intra se Deo agit solennia, cujus cogitatio confitetur ei, et reliquiæ cogitationis ejus diem festum exhibent ipsi, ita quod Deo in mentali quiete solenniter vacat, et dicere potest : In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam; et rursus, Adhæsit anima mea post te.
paras.en: Spiritually: [[2:2|in the seventh month|In septimo mense]], that is, in the rest of the mind, [[2:2|the word of the Lord came by the hand of Haggai|verbum Domini in manu Aggæi]]: namely to him who keeps solemn feasts to God within himself, whose thought gives praise to him, and the remainders of whose thought keep holiday to him[[Ps 75:11||]], so that in the quiet of his mind he is solemnly at leisure for God [*vacat*: he is free and empty for God alone, as on a sabbath], and can say: [[Ps 4:9|In peace in the self same I will sleep, and I will rest|In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam]]; and again, [[Ps 62:9|My soul hath stuck close to thee|Adhæsit anima mea post te]].

paras.t: Loquere ad Zorobabel ducem Juda, et Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum, id est ad principes et prælatos fidelium confitentium Deo, et ad reliquos populi, id est electos, qui respectu reproborum perpauci sunt.
paras.en: [[2:3|Speak to Zorobabel|Loquere ad Zorobabel]] [[2:3|the governor of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest|ducem Juda, et Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum]], that is, to the princes and prelates of the faithful who confess God, [[2:3|and to the rest of the people|et ad reliquos populi]], that is, to the elect, who in respect of the reprobate are very few.

paras.t: Quis in vobis est derelictus, qui vidit domum istam in gloria sua prima, id est, qui consideravit statum Ecclesiæ pro tempore illo quo fuit in maxima sanctitate et gratia, dum fulsit miraculis atque innumeris donis Spiritus Sancti, præsertim tempore Apostolorum, et quod vos videtis hanc nunc, id est, quam vehementer eam nunc lapsam conspicitis, quando omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt? Numquid non ita est, quasi non sit? id est, nullius perfectionis et decoris esse videtur per comparationem ad perfectionem, quam habuit olim.
paras.en: [[2:4|Who is left among you, that saw this house in its first glory|Quis in vobis est derelictus, qui vidit domum istam in gloria sua prima]], that is, who has considered the state of the Church at that time when it was in the greatest holiness and grace, when it shone with miracles and with countless gifts of the Holy Ghost, above all in the time of the Apostles, [[2:4|and how do you see it now|et quod vos videtis hanc nunc]] [the print reads *quod* here, with a footnote giving *quid*, the Vulgate's reading], that is, how very fallen you now behold it, when [[Phil 2:21|all seek the things that are their own|omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt]]? [[2:4|is it not in comparison to that as nothing|Numquid non ita est, quasi non sit]]? that is, it seems to be of no perfection and beauty in comparison with the perfection which it once had.

paras.t: Nihilo minus Dominus erigit corda eorum qui Ecclesiæ deflent ruinam, dicens se esse cum eis. Verbum quod pepigi vobiscum, puta promissio gratiæ atque divini auxilii in præsenti, vel sermo novi Testamenti et evangelicæ legis impletio ac doctrina, quum egrederemini de terra Ægypti, id est de hoc sæculo nequam, seu conversatione carnali, tenebrosa et sæculari, vel quando in Baptismo abrenuntiastis diabolo. Et spiritus meus erit in medio vestrum. Nam Spiritus Sanctus et novi Testamenti pactum, gratia atque subsidium, manent in mentibus electorum, sicut ait Apostolus : Misit Deus Spiritum suum in corda nostra. Et Christus in Evangelio : Paracletus, inquit, Spiritus Sanctus, quem mittet Pater in nomine meo, ille docebit vos omnia.
paras.en: Nevertheless the Lord raises up the hearts of those who weep over the ruin of the Church, saying that he is with them. [[2:6|The word that I covenanted with you|Verbum quod pepigi vobiscum]]: that is, the promise of grace and of divine help in the present, or the word of the New Testament, and the fulfilment and teaching of the law of the Gospel; [[2:6|when you came out of the land of Egypt|quum egrederemini de terra Ægypti]], that is, out of this wicked world, or out of a carnal, dark and worldly way of life, or when in Baptism you renounced the devil. [[2:6|and my spirit shall be in the midst of you|Et spiritus meus erit in medio vestrum]]. For the Holy Ghost, and the covenant, grace and help of the New Testament, abide in the minds of the elect, as the Apostle says: [[Gal 4:6|God hath sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts|Misit Deus Spiritum suum in corda nostra]] [Denis has "his Spirit into our hearts"; the Apostle writes "the Spirit of his Son into your hearts"]. And Christ in the Gospel: [[John 14:26|the Paraclete|Paracletus]], he says, [[John 14:26|the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things|Spiritus Sanctus, quem mittet Pater in nomine meo, ille docebit vos omnia]].

paras.t: Commovebo cælum et terram, imminente finali judicio, sicut expositum est, et movebo omnes gentes. Maxima nempe erit motio atque turbatio hominum tempore Antichristi et in consummatione mundi, juxta illud Danielis : Veniet tempus quale non fuit ex eo, ex quo gentes esse cœperunt, usque ad tempus illud. Et veniet ad finale judicium cum majestate et gloria, Desideratus cunctis gentibus, videlicet Christus, cujus adventus erit electis desiderabilis ac jucundus, quemadmodum ipse hortatur : His, inquiens, fieri incipientibus, levate capita vestra, quoniam appropinquat redemptio vestra. Et implebo domum istam gloria : tunc enim implebitur beatitudine sempiterna.
paras.en: [[2:7|I will move the heaven and the earth|Commovebo cælum et terram]], when the final judgment is at hand, as has been explained, [[2:8|and I will move all nations|et movebo omnes gentes]]. For there will be the greatest commotion and disturbance of men in the time of Antichrist and at the consummation of the world, according to that word of Daniel: [[Dan 12:1|a time shall come, such as never was from the time that nations began, even until that time|Veniet tempus quale non fuit ex eo, ex quo gentes esse cœperunt, usque ad tempus illud]]. And there [[2:8|SHALL COME|Et veniet]] to the final judgment, with majesty and glory, [[2:8|THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS|Desideratus cunctis gentibus]], namely Christ, whose coming will be desirable and joyful to the elect, as he himself exhorts them: [[Luke 21:28|when these things|His]], he says, [[Luke 21:28|begin to come to pass|fieri incipientibus]], [[Luke 21:28|lift up your heads, because your redemption is at hand|levate capita vestra, quoniam appropinquat redemptio vestra]]. [[2:8|and I will fill this house with glory|Et implebo domum istam gloria]]: for then it will be filled with everlasting beatitude.

paras.t: Meum est argentum, et meum est aurum, id est omne spirituale ornamentum quo decoretur Ecclesia, scilicet divitiæ salutis, sapientia et scientia, dotes animarum et corporum.
paras.en: [[2:9|The silver is mine, and the gold is mine|Meum est argentum, et meum est aurum]]: that is, every spiritual adornment with which the Church is to be adorned, namely [[Is 33:6|riches of salvation, wisdom and knowledge|divitiæ salutis, sapientia et scientia]], the dowries of souls and of bodies [*dotes*: the endowments of the blessed in glory, such as the vision of God in the soul and impassibility and brightness in the risen body].

paras.t: Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ, id est, Ecclesiæ triumphantis quam militantis. Fideles quoque qui sub Antichristi persecutione constantes permanserint, maximi meriti erunt; sed major est gratia Dei in Ecclesia tempore evangelicæ legis, quam fuerat sub veteri Testamento. Et in loco isto dabo pacem. Tunc enim pax Christi, quæ omnem sensum exsuperat, implebit Ecclesiam, cujus fines Deus posuit pacem, secundum quod per Isaiam testatur : Ponam visitationem tuam pacem. In patria namque erit perfecta tranquillitas optimæ ordinationis, et plena quies Beatorum in Deo, eritque omnis potentialitas redacta in actum.
paras.en: [[2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first|Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ]]: that is, of the Church triumphant than of the Church militant. The faithful, too, who remain steadfast under the persecution of Antichrist will be of very great merit; but the grace of God in the Church in the time of the law of the Gospel is greater than it had been under the Old Testament. [[2:10|and in this place I will give peace|Et in loco isto dabo pacem]]. For then the peace of Christ, [[Phil 4:7|which surpasseth all understanding|quæ omnem sensum exsuperat]], will fill the Church, whose borders God has made peace[[Ps 147:3||]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 14, by the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 147:3], according to what he testifies by Isaias: [[Is 60:17|I will make thy visitation peace|Ponam visitationem tuam pacem]]. For in the fatherland there will be the perfect tranquillity of the best ordering, and the full rest of the Blessed in God, and every potentiality will be brought into act [that is, every capacity of the creature for good will be wholly fulfilled, with nothing left unrealized].

paras.t: Præterea, juxta propheticam interrogationem, quemadmodum contactus vestimenti in quo sunt carnes sanctificatæ, non sanctificat alia; sic quidam qui se exteriorum rerum sacrarum aut vasorum contactu purgari confidunt, manent polluti, nec interiores suos affectus habuerunt secundum divinam legem reformatos ac ordinatos. Iterum sicut pollutus suo tactu maculat alium, sic qui proximum scandalizat, inficit ipsum.
paras.en: Moreover, according to the prophet's question: as the touch of a garment in which sanctified flesh is carried does not sanctify other things, so certain men who trust to be cleansed by touching outward sacred things or vessels remain defiled, and have not had their inward affections reformed and set in order according to the divine law. Again, as one who is defiled stains another by his touch, so he who scandalizes his neighbour infects him.

paras.t: Et nunc ponite corda vestra a die hac et supra, antequam poneretur lapis super lapidem in templo Domini : id est, pensate quales dudum fuistis, antequam ædificaretis Deo intra vos conscientiæ domum, et antequam in domo hac poneretis lapidem super lapidem, id est unam virtutem, ejusque operationem super aliam, in bonis ordinate crescendo. Tunc utique labores vestri inanes fuerunt, et vix pro media parte tam fructuosi fuerunt, sicut nunc sunt. Et si fructuosi fuerunt, hoc erat ex sola superabundanti bonitate divinæ clementiæ de congruo, non de condigno, eo quod Deus ob suam prorsus immensam pietatem nullum bonum deserat irremuneratum.
paras.en: [[2:16|And now consider in your hearts, from this day and upward, before there was a stone laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord|Et nunc ponite corda vestra a die hac et supra, antequam poneretur lapis super lapidem in templo Domini]]: that is, weigh what you were formerly, before you built within yourselves the house of conscience for God, and before you laid stone upon stone in this house, that is, one virtue and its working upon another, growing in good things in due order. Then indeed your labours were empty, and scarcely half as fruitful as they are now. And if they were fruitful, this came from the sole superabundant goodness of the divine clemency, *de congruo*, not *de condigno* [that is, as something fitting for God's liberality to give, not as a reward owed in justice to merit], because God, of his wholly boundless loving-kindness, leaves no good unrewarded.

paras.t: Insuper percutit nos Deus vento urente tentationum, et opera nostra percuti sinit ac destrui aurugine et grandine adversitatum et persecutionum : nec tamen ad ipsum revertimur, gratiæ opem humiliter implorando.
paras.en: Furthermore, God strikes us [[2:18|with a blasting wind|vento urente]] of temptations, and suffers our works to be struck and destroyed [[2:18|with the mildew and with hail|aurugine et grandine]] of adversities and persecutions; and yet we do not return to him, humbly imploring the help of his grace.

paras.t: Porro, quum nos ipsos cœperimus divino cultui mancipare, et Deo intra nos templum construere, promittitur nobis magna meritorum fecunditas, copiosusque spiritualis profectus, secundum quod subditur : Numquid jam semen in germine est? Semen est verbum Dei, seu gratia Spiritus Sancti : quod tunc in germine est, dum procedit in opus. Sed antequam sic procedat in actum, Deus prædicit se excitaturum illud in opus, quia ad meritorie operandum non solum gratia habituali, sed etiam actuali motione Spiritus Sancti egemus. Et adhuc vinea, id est fides quæ potus est animæ, et ficus, id est caritas sancta, infusa, vere suavis, et malogranatum, id est sacra doctrina vario modo distincta, fortiter odoris optimi diffusiva, et lignum olivæ, id est virtus misericordiæ, non floruit : id est, virtutes istæ et dona Spiritus Sancti, necdum in pulcherrimos operationum ornatus prodierunt. Ex die ista, qua bonum propositum concepistis me inspirante, benedicam, id est, gratiam multiplicabo in vobis, efficaciamque procedendi in actus virtuosos ac splendidos condonabo.
paras.en: But when we have begun to give ourselves over to the worship of God and to build a temple to God within us, great fruitfulness of merits and abundant spiritual progress are promised us, according to what follows: [[2:20|Is the seed as yet sprung up|Numquid jam semen in germine est]]? [[Luke 8:11|The seed is the word of God|Semen est verbum Dei]], or the grace of the Holy Ghost; and it is sprung up [*in germine*, "in the shoot"] when it goes forth into deed. But before it so goes forth into act, God foretells that he will stir it up into deed, because for working meritoriously we need not only habitual grace but also the actual motion of the Holy Ghost [habitual grace is the abiding gift that makes the soul holy; actual grace is a passing movement from God that moves it to act]. [[2:20|or hath the vine|Et adhuc vinea]], that is, faith, which is the drink of the soul, [[2:20|and the fig tree|et ficus]], that is, holy charity, infused, truly sweet, [[2:20|and the pomegranate|et malogranatum]], that is, sacred doctrine, divided in various ways, spreading abroad most powerfully the best of fragrance, [[2:20|and the olive tree|et lignum olivæ]], that is, the virtue of mercy, [[2:20|as yet flourished|non floruit]]? that is, these virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost have not yet come forth into the most beautiful adornments of works. [[2:20|from this day|Ex die ista]], on which you conceived a good purpose by my inspiration, [[2:20|I will bless you|benedicam]], that is, I will multiply grace in you, and will grant you the power of going forward into virtuous and splendid acts.

paras.t: In die illa assumam te, Zorobabel serve meus, et ponam te quasi signaculum, quia te elegi, dicit Dominus. Quotidie Deus impiis et præscitis juste relictis, electos assumit clementer ad gratiam, ornatque eos variis donis atque virtutibus; electos quoque aliorum rectores vicissim tanto gratiarum splendore venustat, ut tanquam signacula subditis merito objiciantur adspiciendi ac imitandi. Totumque hoc efficit Dominus, quia elegit hos quibus hoc præstat. Ipse equidem sine omni merito nostro prior dilexit nos, elegit et prædestinavit quos voluit, secundum quod in Exodo loquitur : Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit. […]
paras.en: [[2:24|In that day|In die illa]] [[2:24|I will take thee, O Zorobabel|assumam te, Zorobabel]] [[2:24|my servant|serve meus]], [[2:24|and will make thee as a signet|et ponam te quasi signaculum]], [[2:24|for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord|quia te elegi, dicit Dominus]]. Daily God, justly leaving aside the wicked and the foreknown [*præsciti*: those whom God foreknows will not be saved], mercifully takes up the elect to grace, and adorns them with various gifts and virtues; and those of the elect who in their turn are rulers of others he beautifies with such splendour of graces that they are rightly set before their subjects as signets, to be looked upon and imitated. And all this the Lord does because he has chosen those to whom he grants it. He indeed, without any merit of ours, [[1 John 4:10|hath first loved us|prior dilexit nos]], has chosen[[Eph 1:4||]] and predestinated[[Eph 1:5||]] whom he would, according to what he says in Exodus: [[Ex 33:19|I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be merciful to whom it shall please me|Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit]] [the margin gives Exod. xxiii, 19; the words are Ex 33:19].
